stem:
The figure shows Sonia's garden plot: rectangle $ABCD$ is $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ by $5\ \mathrm{cm}$, and right triangle $AEB$ has base $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ and height $4\ \mathrm{cm}$ on top of the rectangle.

How should she find the area of the figure?

options.text: Add the rectangle area $10\times 5$ and the triangle area $\dfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times 4$.
Use only the rectangle area $10\times 5$, because the triangle sits on the rectangle.
Multiply the rectangle area by the triangle area to get the composite area.
Any closed garden plot has area $10\times 5$.

teacher.key_rationale: Partition into rectangle 10×5 and triangle ½×10×4, then add. Omitting the triangle, multiplying part areas, or treating every plot as 10×5 miss the composite plan.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite as rectangle ABCD 10 by 5 with triangle AEB of height 4 on top.
